Both letters attack a powerful industry lobby for misleading the public about pending legislation, distinguish ordinary members of the represented industry from their self-appointed or paid spokesmen, emphasize that informed citizens will see through the propaganda, and frame enactment as serving the common welfare. C13 is closer in date and legislative subject, while C03 shares price controls and housewives, but neither matches the child's distinctive anti-lobby architecture as closely as C10.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"They know the lobbyists are working hard here in Washington to get the Congress to pass weak control laws...","parent_excerpt":"I have been shocked in recent days at the extraordinary propaganda campaign that has been unleashed against this bill by the real estate lobby.","explanation":"Both portray an organized lobby as attempting to obstruct or weaken urgently needed legislation before Congress."},{"child_excerpt":"Most of the cattlemen and most of the businessmen are good patriotic Americans...","parent_excerpt":"I know that most of the people engaged in the real estate business and the home building industry in this country are decent, respectable, honorable citizens.","explanation":"This is a distinctive shared move separating ordinary industry members from the lobby acting in their name."},{"child_excerpt":"It must be hard, sometimes, not to identify them all with their self-styled \"spokesmen\" in Washington... the paid propagandists","parent_excerpt":"But there is a little group of ruthless men, claiming to speak for the members of these industries...","explanation":"Both specifically deny that lobbying spokesmen genuinely represent the broader occupational group."},{"child_excerpt":"I don't think you can fool most Americans once they have the facts.","parent_excerpt":"But I do not believe the people of our country, nor their representatives in the Congress, will permit themselves to be deceived. The facts speak for themselves.","explanation":"The closely parallel language expresses the same concluding premise: facts will prevent the public from being deceived by lobby propaganda."}]}
